summary: The TUI chat now gets only the 1,024-item window, so the background prefix conversion cannot reach older history and scrollback before the window is lost.
Once the window slides, the chat's index-based scroll anchor points at a different entry, so a user reading scrollback is moved forward on each update.

The dashboard rebuilds unread agent-message and restart counts from the truncated transcript and overwrites the full counts, so unread items before the window are dropped without the read cursor moving.
When one turn has more than 1,024 items, the dashboard finds no user message in the window, so it clears the 'You' excerpt and drops the current-turn activity preview.

The SQL path for latest_user_position skips user items with no visible text, while the full path and the old latest_completed_turn_ordinal count every user item, so the recovery observer can get an older turn.
Claim that the review seed is now built from the truncated poller projection.
The COUNT(*) and the first/last-user queries still do index work that grows with history on each poll.
Claim that the browser transcript loses visible lines because raw-only entries fill the 1,024-item window.
Claim that the first-user-message query misses user items whose stable ID lacks a user: or user- prefix.
The new test claims the latest user message is outside the window, but the slice keeps it, so the long-turn case is not tested.
Claim that ProjectionWindow::of repeats provisional-title work on every StandaloneSession::snapshot.

The diff deletes the only test of the worker's dispatch gate across a harness restart (closed on HarnessRestarting, reopened on SessionConfigured). That test was the regression test for a production defect.

The diff deletes the only check that the embedded Codex and Claude npm package files match the runtime pins, so a pin bump that misses those files would install old versions under the new install_id without any test failing.
The diff deletes the only worker-startup test that a restart with an existing relay and no review baseline does not create one, which would hide pending work from review.
Deleting the project-memory baseline and replica round-trip test leaves the worker handler's mapping untested.
Deleting the child handback socket test leaves the MCP-to-worker handback request untested.
Deleting the wait return_when test leaves forwarding of return_when 'any' unchecked.
Deleting the reviewer fast-mode test leaves no check that reviewer startup applies fast-mode=on when advertised and continues when the bridge rejects it.
After a steer, the stream emits turn_started for the queued prompt B, but the later completion names the original command A with no accepted ordinal, so B never gets a matching turn_ended.
mj events awaits stdout write_all/flush outside the ctrl_c select, and Tokio's SIGINT handler has replaced default termination, so Ctrl-C is ignored while a piped consumer stops reading.
The activity recorder is an arm of run_server's select!, so any recorder write error ends the whole phone/API server until a daemon restart.
The api_events tables were added without advancing SCHEMA_VERSION, so an older schema-28 build can open the upgraded store and project relay events without journaling them.

When a relay becomes unreachable, the republished view has connected=false, but the viewer projection ignores that, so the recorded activity never changes and the stream keeps reporting the last state.
The activity recorder runs only inside run_server, so with [phone].enabled=false or a failed phone start no activity_changed events are recorded and later replay has a gap.
input_resolved takes turn_id from the turn active when the answer arrives, so a question raised with no turn and answered during a prompt gets inconsistent turn ids.
The '(?2 IS NULL OR e.session_id = ?2)' form keeps SQLite from using api_events_session, so a filtered replay walks the global seq range and can scan all other sessions' history.
repair_projection resets the materialized session to genesis or a checkpoint but leaves api_events, so catch-up re-derives old events and inserts them again with new seq numbers.
A standard SSE reconnect keeps the original ?after_seq and sends a newer Last-Event-ID, which the handler rejects with 400, so replaying EventSource clients cannot resume.
A live-only stream gets no SSE id until its first matching event, so a reconnect before that point starts at a new frontier and silently skips events from the gap.
When a follow-only mj events stream ends before printing any event, the error advises '--after-seq 0', which replays the whole history the user chose to skip.
When an accepted POST /sessions fails provisioning and cleanup succeeds, the provisional session row is deleted, so no launch error is ever journaled for event subscribers.
A close whose checkpoint fails writes last_checkpoint_error and restores the previous state, but the new triggers watch only last_error, so the stream gets no error event for the failed close.

The wrapped quota row requests its full height with no bound, so in the 20-row inline viewport (and short fullscreen terminals) it competes with the live tail and input, and quota or transcript rows get cut off.
The new test draws draw_usage_quota_row into its own 50x5 area and does not exercise the full inline/fullscreen layouts.

resolve_repository marks every resolve_local_repository error as a missing-remote Refusal, so Git spawn failures, timeouts and cancellation become a 409 'configure a remote' instead of a 500 with a log reference.
A capacity refresh that finds the poller stopped returns a 500 citing log reference 'capacity-poller', but nothing logs that reference.
LifecycleFailure::into_error rebuilds the error as Error::new(refusal).context(detail), but detail already contains the refusal sentence, so {error:#} prints it twice.
Claims the missing-remote refusal surfaces only after the new session was accepted, so it cannot reach the caller.

The RecoverFailed dialog appends its buttons after an unbounded wrapped error and does not scroll, so a long error or a short terminal pushes the actions, including the default-focused Recover, out of view.

'Open transcript' on an Error session sends DashboardAction::Open, which needs a session-manager actor, but Error sessions are excluded from worker targets, so the open fails with 'session ... is not managed'.
Reports that no new test activates the Recover button.
Answering a turn-review form calls poll_turn_review_role, which starts a second self-rescheduling poll loop for a role that is already being polled, so each answer permanently adds a loop.

An answered reviewer form can be shown again if any poll returns before its ElicitationResolved event reaches the pane; the reopened dialog never closes, and answering it again fails the whole turn review.
handle_mouse still sends clicks and scrolls to the review split under an open reviewer dialog, so a click can hit a hidden review action such as Cancel.
Metadata-only archives keep schema 10 (review refs), so an older reader that accepts schema 10 ignores the new flag and fails on missing objects or checks out contents.

collect_git_metadata_snapshot sets review_refs_metadata_only only when refs/mj refs exist, so a raw capture without refs still restores as a full snapshot and can check out or rewind the shared checkout.

Once the destination-baseline refusal is gone, a raw resume into a checkout whose baseline pin belongs to another session skips the pin, and worker startup may then replace it, losing both sessions' baselines.
A prompt submitted while a config update is in flight is discarded by the runtime, but the UI has already recorded it and set turn=Streaming, so the UI stays stuck in Streaming.

refresh_config_picker keeps the selected option and value as list positions, so a ConfigOptionUpdate that removes or reorders entries while the value picker is open can make Enter apply a different setting or value.
The picker modal height is desired_rows + 4, but the chrome needs 5 rows (2 borders, a 2-row header, a 1-row footer), so the list always gets one row fewer than intended.
On a terminal 8 rows tall or shorter, the picker modal is not drawn but config_picker stays open and takes every key, so users can move and apply choices they cannot see.

Cancelling a workspace close calls cancel_lifecycle on each original session ID, which can abort an unrelated operation, such as a Resume into another workspace, started after that session finished stopping.
When one dashboard closes the default workspace, other connected dashboards never discard their cached composers for its sessions, so the discarded text can reappear.
discard_workspace_composers does not clear DashboardState::standby_prompts, so standby text survives a confirmed workspace close and is restored when the session is later opened.
If the follow-up runtime snapshot or workspace-list load fails after a successful close_workspace, the whole close is reported as failed and deleted_workspace_id is lost.
A Cancel sent while the close request is still connecting can reach the daemon before close_workspace registers its cancel flag; the cancel is refused and the close then runs to completion.

After cancellation, a root job's close_session keeps starting stops for the remaining children and the parent without checking the workspace cancel flag; only the 100 ms poll can cancel them afterwards.

The final cancel check runs before the deletion is queued on the database writer, so a cancel accepted while the write is queued is reported as requested but the workspace and its drafts are still deleted.

If the close command is reopened while its close is running, and the reopened manager's load arrives after the close result, the stale load opens a fresh close confirmation for a workspace that has already been deleted.

A non-in-place Move is durably Stopped during source cleanup and destination preflight; workspace close neither sees nor waits for it, so the workspace can be deleted under the Move, which then fails to restore the session.
A tight nested list merges the parent and child text on one line under the child marker, because entering the nested list does not flush the parent's pending spans and prefix.
Rich mode discards Markdown link destinations (including ACP resource-link URIs) and shows only an underlined label with no hyperlink or open action.
A header-only Markdown table that is wider than the viewport renders nothing, because the record fallback skips the header row and there are no body rows.
Grid-mode table rows are joined without per-column padding, so column separators do not line up when cell widths differ.
wrap_styled_graphemes compares a grapheme count with a column width, so a first row containing wide characters can be dropped when a narrow-table record wraps.
Streamed chunks are sanitized one at a time, so a CRLF or ANSI escape split across chunks becomes an extra newline or leaves escape fragments in the text.
Tool location paths are not passed through sanitize_terminal_text, unlike tool titles and content, and are shown in raw mode.
After a soft break inside a list item, the continuation line loses the item's indent because finish_line consumes item_prefix on the first line.
The ignored Docker test asserts agent-dev:latest has no image worker, which stops being true once this change publishes :latest with /opt/mjolnir/mj-worker.

Worker recovery and parked sub-agent wake still resolve a host worker and digest-compare it with the linked image worker, so they replace the link with a host copy or fail when no host worker is available.
Claim that '!mj-core/' after '**' re-includes only the directory entry, so crate sources are excluded from the build context.
A dangling symlink at /opt/mjolnir/mj-worker is reported as absent because the probe uses test -e.
build-agent-dev-image.sh stamps an image built from uncommitted worker sources with the committed identity.
build-agent-dev-image.sh uses tomllib, which needs Python 3.11 or newer.

A development build with uncommitted worker edits reports the same build ID as the image, so container sessions run the image's unmodified worker and ignore the locally built one, including MJ_WORKER_BINARY.
The local-build command in mj-controller/docs/PODMAN.md now fails because the Containerfile requires build arguments the command does not pass.
The new close-failure recovery dialog is never opened in production, and the dashboard's direct `x` force-destroy key was removed, so force destroy becomes unreachable from the dashboard.

The new lossy annotation makes cross-harness resume choices wrap, but render_picker still sizes the popup at one row per choice and never scrolls, so later choices and the help lines are clipped while still selectable.
Streamed chunks still join words, because update_activity runs truncate_text (which collapses whitespace and drops trailing spaces) after every append.

In the agent-dev image, the clean login environment drops the Rust base image's RUSTUP_HOME and CARGO_HOME, and the new profile.d file does not restore them, so rustup proxies look in /home/hel/.rustup.
Custom container images that expose bridges or MUSE_CLI through Dockerfile ENV lose those values after the clean re-exec.

The GH_TOKEN that provisioning injects into the container is cleared by the re-exec before configure_github_cli copies it to the worker's github-token file, so new container sessions have no GitHub token until credential sync runs.

The standalone `worker push-branch` now re-execs clean, so it loses the container's GH_TOKEN, which the `!gh auth git-credential` helper relied on. It also never attaches the session's token file or Git wrapper, so branch pushes to private GitHub remotes fail.
local-bare workers no longer inherit GH_TOKEN, GITHUB_TOKEN or GIT_SSH_COMMAND from the daemon environment.
scripts/run.sh now needs `node` to pick the built mj executable, and the source-build instructions do not list Node.
ACP terminal spawns remove GH_TOKEN/GITHUB_TOKEN even when the terminal request supplies them explicitly.
If the image user's passwd shell is /sbin/nologin, the mandatory login capture runs nologin and the worker fails to start.

GIT_CONFIG_COUNT and its indexed entries, which configure_github_cli moves out of the session environment, are added back when the cached login baseline is merged again at the supervisor and ACP launch.
The login capture runs `<shell> -l -c`, which csh and tcsh reject, and login capture is now mandatory for sessions, diffs and pushes.
The clean re-exec drops XDG_CACHE_HOME and the MJ_TEST_HOOK/MJ_TEST_HOOK_DIR/MJ_CHAOS_ISOLATED variables that the reliability and hook-chaos e2e labs pass through the worker's inherited environment.
Diff and PushBranch re-exec with a clean environment but do not get the target's configured environment, so container settings such as PATH, proxy or GIT_SSH_COMMAND are lost for those helpers.
SSH_AUTH_SOCK from the launching session is cleared, so worker Git operations that rely on an ssh-agent lose access to it.
The ExecPlan's completed Progress entries have no timestamps.

The custom-image documentation still says worker commands do not source login files, that the ordinary process PATH is enough, and that `!command` runs through `bash -lc`. This diff reverses all three.
`!` user shell commands changed from `bash -lc` to `bash -c`, so functions and other non-exported state from Bash login files are no longer available.
After a poll failure, rehydration installs a summary unread count that already includes messages still held in unread_agent_message_sequences, and the row adds both, double-counting them.
Hydrating only a 10-entry tail with last_agent_message unset lets the Delete key skip the DESTROY confirmation and force-destroy sessions whose assistant replies fall outside the tail.

WorkerPollTarget.viewed_through is not refreshed after chat exit marks the session viewed, so a later reconnect asks for a summary with the stale cursor and already-read messages show as unread again.

The full-history bootstrap on open moves the client cursor past TurnCompleted events without sending them to recovery_context, and run_chat(Some(chat)) skips its own bootstrap observation, so automatic recovery can miss a completed turn.
Opening a warm v3 session now runs a full multi-page replay inline in the dashboard event loop, which blocks input and termination and cannot be cancelled.

The worker's unread count uses started_seq from a whitespace-only first chunk, while live dashboard polling ignores blank chunks, so the two unread predicates disagree when the user detaches between the blank chunk and the text.
Claims set_state keeps the full summarized unread count after a partial view.
The new 'No messages yet' placeholder is unreachable because hydration always stores Some(transcript), so an empty conversation renders blank.
Summary hydration counts unread messages for the selected session even when its conversation is on screen, unlike the event path, which suppresses visible messages.
Rehydration after a reconnect resets current_turn_started_at to now and bumps last_activity_at even with no new events, which zeroes the turn timer and reorders sessions by recent activity.
Per-file model downloads no longer provide test_wavs/, so on a fresh cache the ignored end-to-end test dictation_models_install_and_decode_test_wav panics at expect("list test_wavs").
Removing extract_tar_bz2_file removed the only use of the bzip2 crate, but the dependency stays in Cargo.toml.
The setup status is put into the input block title before the percentage and the 'Ctrl-R stop' hint, so narrower terminals clip the progress and the stop hint.

Concurrent installers share a fixed '<file>.part' temp path. One worker can unlink and recreate the other's temp file and then rename an unfinished download into place, where has_model_data accepts it as installed.
Claims dictation setup status is hidden while an agent turn is busy, because busy_prompt_title takes precedence.
Before microphone levels arrive, dictation_prompt_title shows any Info status_line, so an unrelated notice such as Ctrl-Y's clipboard message replaces the setup progress.
megabytes() truncates to whole MiB, so downloads of sub-MB files such as tokens.txt report 'N% of 0 MB'.

The runtime task records Failed directly when acp::run returns Err, while Started is recorded only after SessionStarted travels through the orchestrator and the outer select loop, so a session that starts and then exits quickly can be permanently recorded as a launch failure.
begin() evicts the oldest record regardless of state, so 64 newer launches remove a still-Starting record; its outcome is then dropped and the viewer gets 404s until its generic timeout.
An unbounded launch-status fetch could stall the watcher before refreshSessions.
No ownership recheck after the new status await before refreshSessions/navigation.
An adapter that never answers initialize/session/new leaves the launch Starting until the viewer's timeout.

When session/load (no resume capability) fails with the missing-thread error, the fallback to session/new never enables session_updates_enabled, so every update from the replacement thread is dropped.

Pre-upgrade snapshots read native_session_used=false, and the earlier SessionOpened{resumed:true} sits below the snapshot frontier, so an imported/resumed thread with no local prompts and floor 0 is classed unused and replaced when its rollout is missing.
A queued prompt the user removes or clears becomes Rejected without being sent, and the new predicate counts any non-Queued/Pending Prompt as history, which blocks replacement of an unused thread.
A successful resume marks the durable flag but not the bridge's in-memory native_session_used, so an in-process bridge restart could replace the thread.

File export passes the layout's workspace_root (the parent of a bare session's project directory) as the read boundary, so sibling files such as ~/.ssh/id_rsa or other sessions' worktrees are readable and ordinary checkout-relative paths resolve one directory too high.

Bundle export for a managed bare worktree always refuses with 'no commits beyond the session base' because the checkpoint captures DeltaFrom the worktree's current HEAD, so its committed bundle is always empty.
Bundle export for an unmanaged bare checkout always refuses because its checkpoint is MetadataOnly.

For a session whose project directory is a repository subdirectory, session_diff stages only `.` into an empty scratch index, so the captured tree lacks everything outside the subdirectory and the patch shows those files as deleted.
Tracked files that match an ignore rule are left out of the empty scratch index, so the session diff against the committed base reports them as deleted.

session_diff reuses diff_between_trees, which decodes Git's patch with String::from_utf8_lossy, so non-UTF-8 text in a changed file is silently replaced and the exported patch no longer reproduces the change.
Diff export for an unmanaged bare checkout (including an existing linked worktree) sends no base or branch, so session_diff refuses with 'no session base recorded'.
The reflog fallback treats the oldest remaining reflog entry as the branch creation point, so after the creation entry expires the diff silently uses a later commit and omits earlier session work.
A file path or branch beginning with '-' is passed as a separate argv value after --path/--branch, clap rejects it with exit 2, and the API misreports that the worker predates export support.

push-branch runs in a fresh worker process without the session's GitHub credential environment (gh wrapper and GIT_CONFIG helpers), so HTTPS pushes fail on targets that rely on Mjolnir's synchronized token.
require_idle_turn treats a missing actor or snapshot as idle and trusts a cached view, with nothing that holds off a new turn, so a push can run while a just-submitted turn is starting.
checkpoint_session_now only checks for active lifecycle work and registers nothing, so two bundle exports, or a bundle export and a close or move, can checkpoint the same session concurrently.
A live bundle export awaits Controller::checkpoint_session directly on the async runtime, and its synchronous ProcessExecutor and file work blocks a Tokio worker for the whole checkpoint.
A stopped Podman session keeps target: Some until deferred storage cleanup succeeds, so bundle export treats it as live and tries a new checkpoint instead of reading its saved archive.
Claim that bundle export misses session commits already pushed to origin for managed network workspaces.

Moving a bundle session into a fresh raw worktree records the source checkout's current HEAD as the diff base, while resume restores the archived session head, so the diff includes reversals of unrelated source changes.
read_session_file checks the canonical path and size, then reopens with fs::read, so a concurrent symlink swap or file growth could bypass the checks.
After checkpoint_now returns, a concurrent checkpoint can install a newer archive and prune_replaced_checkpoint can delete this export's archive before verify_repository_bundles_streaming opens it.

The new preview_scrollbar drag state is not cleared by cancel_component_pointer, so a drag interrupted by Delete, Help, a bound command or focus loss stays active and swallows wheel and motion events until the next click.

Title or project matches now come from a metadata-only scan with preview: None, so those rows lose the preview text that the TUI's archived-row details and the web viewer show when there is no snippet.
The new PreviousHit and NextHit buttons can take keyboard focus but are drawn only by their enabled state, so a focused arrow shows no focus marker.
At the minimum 30-column preview width, the [↑] button overwrites the end of the 'hit N/M' title once the count has two digits.
The hit arrow labels are hard-coded Unicode and ignore the ASCII glyph setting.
A scrollbar click or drag that scrolls the preview returns without setting last_event_consumed, so the input batch does not redraw before hit-testing the next mouse event.
Counting hits in prepare rebuilds the preview lines and throws them away.
A reviewer summary that reports no findings; it makes no defect claim.
A checkpoint deferred because the session is busy leaves its uniquely named prestage directory on the target, so repeated deferrals pile up full stage copies.
A deferred manual checkpoint saves last_checkpoint_error = None, which hides an earlier real checkpoint failure even though no new archive was installed.

An idle observation that arrives while a deferred copy still holds the recovery gate is dropped, and abandon_attempt does not re-check it, so the turn can stay without a recovery copy while the session sits idle.
The automatic review only arms when the previous view was prompt-driven, so when coalescing drops the in-between Idle (or active-prompt) view, a completed prompt turn is not reviewed.
A close checkpoint that finds a harness turn started during its export fails as CheckpointDeferred and is not retried.
same_installation now calls std::fs::canonicalize, and Settings' Detect profiles reaches it on the TUI event loop, which breaks the no-blocking-I/O rule and can freeze the UI on a hung mount.

Identity comparison expands a hand-written ~ home, but runtime code uses profile.home literally, so discovery now suppresses the usable absolute-home profile and keeps one that cannot reach its files.
When canonicalize fails, the lexical fallback collapses `link/..` even when `link` is a symlink, so a missing configured home can falsely match a different existing discovered home and suppress it.

A configured home with a missing intermediate directory (`/missing/../home/.claude`) matches the existing discovered home, but on Unix the configured spelling cannot be opened, so the only kept profile is unusable.

When canonicalize fails, the lexical fallback does not resolve symlinked ancestors, so a missing home spelled through a symlinked prefix still does not match its canonical form and the duplicate stays.

For OpenCode/Muse, a symlink or `..` spelling of the stock XDG home now suppresses the stock profile, but is_own_nested_home compares paths as written, so the kept profile uses <home>/.data/<id> and loses the user's existing login.

spawn_config_rename puts the local Controller::load reload inside the 15 s SAVE_ACK_TIMEOUT, so a slow reload after a successful rename is reported as an unacknowledged daemon save and the reload result is dropped.

For a source adapter that has session/resume but not loadSession, the runtime resumes without replaying history yet still emits SessionStarted{resumed:true}, so the import finishes with an empty transcript and a fresh primary.

Input typed or submitted in the temporary import UI is lost: a submitted prompt goes to the source runtime, which is shut down right away, and is then folded into the acknowledge-only handoff. Drafts are dropped.
With a configured reasoning_effort, a same-route /load that falls back to restart is misread as a cross-agent import, because the roster.available entries have reasoning_effort None.

After a cross-agent import, the new primary UI shows only the placeholder 'Session history loaded from the previous primary agent.' The replayed conversation is not in the fullscreen transcript or in /export.

Subagent reports that came back through the mj-subagents subagent_cancel tool result are missing from the import handoff, because replayed transport tool calls are suppressed and replay does not rebuild the nested subagent transcripts.
SwitchSession finds the source route through a best-effort provenance record keyed by the current cwd, and falls back to the active adapter when no record is found.
ClipboardTarget::Answer holds only the question ID, so Ctrl+V followed by Tab before the read completes pastes into the newly focused answer field.
set_prompt_images_supported bumps input_generation on every capability change, so an in-flight text-only paste (answer or search) is silently dropped and 'Reading clipboard…' stays shown.
A finished image attachment bumps input_generation and so discards a second clipboard read started while it was installing.

Treating 'Cannot connect to the Docker daemon' as NotRunning makes doctor, setup and the wizard say the daemon is stopped and advise starting it when a stale DOCKER_HOST or context points at an unreachable endpoint.
Reviewer reported no findings; this entry claims no defect.

A macOS Claude session started by the earlier release with Mjolnir sub-agents enabled loses all delegation after a worker upgrade or recovery: the refreshed launch sets subagent_tools=true, which removes Agent/Task, but the linked home never received the mj-agents MCP entry.

Checkpoints of a legacy local session whose launch.json was not rewritten fail with 'project memory replica is outside the harness home', because the checkpoint now passes the symlinked <worker_root>/profile while launch.json names the original home, and the check is lexical.

For a legacy macOS Claude session with a non-default profile home, the link points at the recorded harness_home, but the old launch left CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR unset so Claude actually used its default home; relaunch and checkpoint then use a home without the session's transcript.
session_has_a_staged_home_of_its_own adds a synchronous symlink_metadata call per local session inside credential_sync_targets, which the TUI and web server call on their event loops.
docs/src/content/docs/profiles.md still says local sessions and macOS Claude run from the profile home directly and that custom macOS Claude homes are reported as ignored.
A legacy session whose configured profile directory does not exist gets no link, so checkpoint and relaunch point at a missing staged home.

When an admitted session fails or times out during the new readiness wait, session/new returns an error but the ID is already in `sessions`, so unanswered_refusal returns None and the adapter exits 0 even though no session was created.
In the e2e cleanup, one failed or timed-out destroy exits the shared try block, so later sessions are never destroyed and the daemon is then stopped with their workers still running.
A readiness poll that lands while the daemon is being replaced gets a connection error, and session/new fails even though the admitted session may finish starting.

Readiness requires is_idle, which is false during any turn or background command, so a prompt from another client (or background work) during startup can delay session/new and make it time out after 10 minutes although the session started.
The e2e completion check matches the marker text without checking that the update kind is agent_message_chunk.
The fake daemon derives is_idle from other fields, so no test covers a Live/running session whose is_idle is false.
`mj go` in a folder named `default` (any case) now fails, because its separate name chooser does not treat the hidden `default` name as taken and the new store guard refuses the create.
Creating a workspace named `default` through the API returns HTTP 500 because the reserved-name refusal is an untyped anyhow error.
Listing a `default` that holds only suspended sessions lets the user delete or close it, and after the row is gone every prompt-history insert fails the workspace trigger.
If the listed `default` row is renamed and later emptied, it is hidden by its id, and the new guard refuses to create a workspace with the new name.
The missing-workspace refusal prints session_count, which counts only non-stopped sessions, so a `default` listed for its suspended history shows `(0 sessions)`.
`mj new` reads the prompt and checks --bundle/--project-directory before it refuses a missing workspace.
The optional list_workspaces call in the refusal has no timeout.
Daemon connection or listing failures are only logged, and the refusal omits their cause.
The new acp test runs the child with Command::output() instead of a shared subprocess helper.
The new mixed background label (for example '1 task, 1 shell 50s') is wider than the minimized Sessions row, so truncation from the right hides the elapsed clock.
The new confirmation lease is held on the source through validate_move_destination_configuration, whose fresh serialized profile probe can run for minutes, freezing the source actor.
On a retry after queue admission started, execute_move skips drop(source_relay), so the confirmation lease on the now-live destination is held through finish_workspace_transfer and admit_move_queue.

If the held Move lease fails its sync in open_checkpoint_relay (or MoveSourceRelay::sync), the lease is dropped back to the actor before the worker restart, which reopens a confirmation-to-seal admission window.

When the source was not held (unreachable), prepare_move_source_checkpoint restarts it CheckpointOnly and then releases the adopted lease instead of keeping it in source_relay, leaving the actor unleased until the sealing checkpoint leases again.
Holding the actor connection does not freeze work queued inside the worker, so a queued prompt could start before BeginCheckpoint.
No test exercises a held source connection from confirmation through sealing.
owner_only_create_options declares `let mut options` but only mutates it under #[cfg(unix)], so Windows builds hit unused_mut and Windows Clippy with -D warnings fails.
Provisioning creates the worker root with `mkdir -p` (default umask) before the worker runs, so WorkerRootOwner::acquire's 0700 creation mode never applies to newly provisioned roots.
Directories and active.jsonl files that already exist with permissive modes stay readable after upgrade.

Opening the picker from a chip click leaves task_control_focused/subagent_control_focused set, and handle_key checks those flags before the picker, so Enter/Down/Esc go to the task or sub-agent control.
Chip hitboxes are claimed for every mouse kind, so a transcript drag that crosses a chip gets its selection cleared by route_selection.
A chip that does not fully fit gets no hitbox, but ratatui still draws its visible part with chip styling, so the visible control does nothing when clicked.
The chip limit reserves no room for the right-aligned activity title, so spinner cells drawn over a chip's end still open the selector.
When the autocomplete popup falls back to the centred position over the prompt title, retained chip hitboxes win over the popup's cells.
notification_body has no Unreachable arm, so a desktop notification for an unreachable worker shows the last agent message or 'Finished'.
A session with a failed review and an unreachable (or Disconnected) worker is classified Unreachable rather than Failed, because the connectivity return runs before the review check.
The wide form of the minimized Sessions title shows 'Attention: N' without the most-urgent glyph, which only the narrower forms include.

The row's activity text keeps its own precedence (Unreachable, then Question, then review label) and ignores the attention level, so a failed review with a pending question draws × but reads 'Question'.
The new docs say a failed move gets the × Failed badge, but a failed move that leaves the session Stopped is classified Inactive.

muse_data_dir decides whether the profile home is the person's own Muse home by lexical path equality, so a symlinked or otherwise equivalent path to ~/.config/muse looks for the catalog under <home>/.data/muse instead of the XDG data directory.
The new catalog copy shipped without a test, and the removed Muse discovery test was not replaced.
Path::exists() returns false on a permission error, so an inaccessible catalog directory is treated as absent instead of reported.
Already-running Muse sessions do not get the catalog when their worker is upgraded, because worker upgrade does not re-stage the profile.

A prompt that first arrives while the record says running but the prompt capability is still false (handshake done, no first report yet) is refused at once with 409, because waiting starts false and is_coming_up excludes Running.

The loop breaks as soon as capabilities.prompt is true, but a session created with model, effort, or an initial prompt keeps StartStatus::Pending until its follow-up finishes, so backend.prompt fails with 'session initialization is still running' as a 500.
An ACP session/cancel sent while the prompt is held is refused (no turn yet), and the held prompt is submitted anyway after the worker attaches.
The readiness wait does not select on state.shutdown, so on daemon shutdown a held prompt is aborted by the server rather than receiving the 503 the code intends.
The up-to-60-second readiness wait holds no upgrade admission permit, so a daemon handoff can end the request before the prompt is submitted.
Raising the wait in shutdown_all_kills_running_terminal_commands to 60s lets a 30-second command exit naturally, so the test passes even if shutdown_all never kills it.
drive_client_returns_when_command_channel_drops now allows 60s although main.rs aborts the ACP task after 2s, so a shutdown taking 2-60s would pass.

When native_muse_turn panics (event timeout, assertion, or shutdown timeout), it skips Close and the join, so the caller's TempDir is deleted while the adapter and native Muse processes are still running.
The 120s timeout restarts after every event, so a provider that keeps streaming without finishing makes the live test run forever.
The pinned field title is drawn as an unwrapped one-row Paragraph and removed from the scrolling body, so a title wider than the pane loses its end (including ' (required)') with no way to reveal it.
When the body has only two rows, the new budget gives both to the focused field (title + control), so the agent message gets zero rows.

supervise publishes the exit only after both pipe drains reach EOF, so a background descendant that inherits stdout/stderr keeps terminal/wait_for_exit and the output exitStatus pending after the shell has exited.
kill_if_live treats the leader's published exit as proof the process group is gone, so kill, release, shutdown and Drop skip a group that still contains a background child with redirected output.
If the shell is reaped while a descendant that left the group still holds a pipe, exit stays None and a later kill may signal a reused process group ID.

Terminals run in their own process groups with only in-daemon cleanup, so stopping a bare-target worker daemon by signalling its group leaves running terminal commands alive while cleanup deletes their files.
Terminal children get the daemon environment plus request.env only, missing the profile/session environment that is given to the ACP bridge.
TerminalRegistry::shutdown kills and then awaits each terminal in turn with a 5 s timeout, so several stuck supervisors make teardown take 5 s each and leave later groups running meanwhile.
TerminalBuffer::read applies the byte limit before from_utf8_lossy, so invalid UTF-8 expands to U+FFFD and the served output can be up to 3x the requested outputByteLimit, with truncated=false.
output() reads the buffer, releases its lock, then reads the exit watch, so a response can pair a completed exit status with output missing the final bytes.
Each new registry numbers terminals from term-1, so after a worker restart or resume new terminal output is attached to old transcript tool calls with the same ID.

release removes the entry and detaches its supervisor, so connection shutdown does not wait for it and RuntimeEvent::Stopped can arrive before the released terminal's TerminalClosed, which is then never journaled.
shell_line inserts command verbatim into sh -c, so an executable path with spaces or shell metacharacters is parsed as shell syntax.

The session actor is not leased during the connect-time worker restart, so it and the restart's own StandaloneSession both project relay events into the shared DB projection, and adopting the older restart connection after lease_connection() syncs leaves its in-memory frontier behind the DB; either way a sync hits AlreadyApplied and Stop fails again.

While the worker restarts, the unleased actor can deliver a prompt submitted at that moment to the restarted worker instead of deferring it, so Stop can interrupt or archive that work, or wait on it until the post-restart barrier timeout and then fail with no restart left to try.

When the post-restart lease_connection() fails, adopt_restarted_checkpoint_relay continues on a standalone connection, so a managed checkpoint or Close runs without the actor's exclusive lease (prompts are not deferred and two projectors compete).

worker_connect_needs_restart does not recognize 'write relay (hello) request: Broken pipe', so when the proxy has already exited at write time, the restart is skipped and Stop fails against the dead worker.

A proxy EOF during hello, which a transient SSH failure can also cause, is taken as proof of a dead worker, so the checkpoint path, including automatic recovery checkpoints, stops and restarts a worker that may still be alive.
The new test checks only the error-string classifier, not the restart and adoption behavior.
Reviewer reported no findings.

The controller's GitHub token is put into podman/container run argv as GH_TOKEN=<token>, and for SSH Podman also into the ssh command line and remote shell command, where other users can read it from process listings.

The container bootstrap now requires `gh` on every managed container, even with no token or no GitHub repositories, so images that have Git but no gh and no root or passwordless sudo now fail provisioning. This includes images built from the previous bundled Containerfile.
A GH_TOKEN set in the target's environment is silently overridden by the controller's token, because the injected --env comes after the configured one.

use_github_https_urls trusts the lax github_repository_from_origin parser, so with a token present a non-GitHub SCP URL such as git@gitlab.com:group/repo is rewritten to https://github.com/git@gitlab.com:group/repo.git.

If the image's global Git config already has a multi-valued credential.https://github.com.helper, as `gh auth setup-git` writes, the plain `git config --global` set fails and `set -e` aborts provisioning.
ReviewDispatch::launch validates the new required per-reviewer hypothesis but then discards it, so the launched specialist never sees the risk it was dispatched to investigate.
The new inline-mode render test uses a fixed 12-row backend, so it does not exercise the desired_inline_height +1 row for a queued steer.
Reports of no findings; no defect is claimed.

The five-second deadline and cancellation flag apply only to subprocesses, so a local completion on a stalled filesystem holds one of the four shared preflight slots until read_dir returns, even after the browser aborts.
Arrow-key navigation changes aria-selected but never scrolls the selected row into the 40dvh list, so Enter can accept a row the user cannot see.
Suggestion rows are default-focusable buttons, so Tab from the input targets the first row, and the input's blur handler removes that row before focus reaches it.
The input has no combobox wiring (no aria-controls, aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant, or row IDs), so screen readers do not announce the path that Enter will insert.

Blur and Escape hide the list but do not clear the debounce timer or abort the in-flight request, so suggestions can appear after Escape, or after the user leaves and comes back, and the abandoned lookup still uses a preflight slot.
The five-second deadline starts only after the request leaves the shared queue, so time spent waiting for a slot is not counted.

In Recover mode, a corrupt line longer than RELAY_EVENT_BYTE_BUDGET (2 MiB) makes read_bounded_line fail before the recovery branch runs, so the whole scan aborts instead of recording a gap and continuing.
The changed visit_relay_journal_file call at src/hel_worker.rs:1921 is 107 columns long and not rustfmt-formatted, so the CI `cargo fmt --check` step fails.
Claim: the Recover variant and the RelayJournalGap fields are dead code in the library build, so `clippy -D warnings` fails.
Claim: a record whose bytes are removed but whose newline stays is skipped as an empty line and not reported as a gap.
Filter edits call clamp_selections, which prunes collapsed_project_keys against project_keys() that now reads the filtered list, so a filter that hides a folded project permanently unfolds it.

When the action row has focus (forced there by an empty filtered list, or by pressing Up), the session_action_focus.is_none() gate stops Esc and the state letters from reaching the non-editing filter handler, so the advertised 'Esc clears the filter' does nothing.
Recent records only commands without pane keys, so Create session or Search sessions run from the palette never appear under Recent.

select_active_session now searches the filtered ordered_sessions(), so Create (and resume) under an active filter that excludes the new session leaves the previous session selected while focus moves to the prompt.

rebuild_palette_entries keeps the selected command by id across query edits; with weak subsequence/description matches now retained, the cursor can stay on a lower-ranked command (e.g. Restart session for 'ren'), and Enter runs it instead of the top match.
Create session is not listed in the palette when it is opened from Workspaces, Targets, or Quota, because scope_order includes only the focused pane's scope.

The d (Done) filter selects an unread session; the surface opens it, acknowledging the reply clears Unread, clamp_selections then drops it and selects the next unread one, so the filter marks replies read without showing them.
Pasted text (bracketed paste or clipboard paste) is dropped while the Sessions search is editing, because handle_paste returns unless a component modal or the Prompt has focus.
Activity, connectivity, and review changes alter filter membership without calling clamp_selections, leaving the selection on a row the filter now hides.
In mj go mode, rows show go_conversation_title (e.g. 'Conversation 1') but the filter matches display_title(), which is the session id, so searching the visible name hides the row.
The filter is cleared on workspace switches but not when opening or closing a sub-agent workspace, so a parent-name search hides every child, and a child search can hide the parent on return.

Legacy Row positions are always read as full-history indexes, but an old build that saved while its prefix was still unconverted wrote a tail-relative index, so such a handoff position restores to the wrong entry.

The saved Entry anchor identifies an entry only by start_seq, but SessionRestarted during a running turn creates the restart marker and the 'Work interrupted' marker with the same position, so a position saved on the second restores to the first.

A chat opened without a snapshot whose initial Sync fails clears transcript_loading, so the next draw treats the empty projection as complete and replaces the pending restore with Bottom; the transcript that arrives on a later retry opens at the tail.
The rename dialog looks the same when the title field has focus and when Save has focus, but typing only works in the field.
Holding Enter to start an import lets a repeated Enter cancel it at once, because Enter now cancels in the progress dialog.
popup_height is said to omit the two border rows, so the import progress popup clips the Cancel button.
The rename paragraph has no wrap, so popup_height cannot grow and long titles or IDs are cut off.
On the native-import branch, `mj resume --wiki <id> --json` prints importer progress to stdout before the JSON object, so the output is not valid JSON.
`mj resume --wiki` hardcodes the import safety acknowledgements to false and has no flags to set them, so a non-interactive import of a session with dirty or omitted roots always fails.

The native import looks up the session ID only in the stock harness home and ignores the indexed path, so sessions indexed from a non-default profile home are reported missing (or a same-ID session in the stock home is imported instead).
A new daemon action and HTTP route were added without bumping PROTOCOL_VERSION, so an upgraded client keeps using the old daemon, which lacks the wiki-session route.
The archived-restore branch sends workspace_id None. The restore route turns it into "" and session registration rejects it, so `mj resume --wiki <archived-id>` fails unless --workspace-id is given.

The native-import branch calls resolve_store_workspace(None) and the resume dispatcher drops the global --workspace, so with several workspaces the command fails and tells the user to pass a flag it ignores.
Archived container or bundle sessions have no indexed project directory, and the CLI sends project_directory None, so restore fails with 'name a project directory'.

After the import is saved, the immediate resume request can reach the HTTP route before the web server's snapshot includes the new session and get a 404, which leaves a stopped imported session behind.
Logout with a correctly signed but expired cookie returns success without recording a revocation, so a renewal response computed just before expiry and delivered after logout restores access.

When saving the revocation ledger fails, the new 500 from logout goes uncaught in viewer.js, the in-memory revocation then sends the viewer to the login screen, and the user gets no error and no way to retry, so the cookie works again after a restart.
The revocation lasts max(presented cookie expiry, now + current TTL), so after session_ttl is reduced, an older cookie issued under the longer TTL can outlive the revocation and authenticate again.
Legacy unmarked cookies are revoked only until the presented cookie's own expiry, so a later-expiring legacy copy issued by the previous build could become valid afterwards.
A request authenticated before cookie expiry but finishing after it no longer renews the cookie, unlike the previous pre-handler renewal.
Event streams opened before logout keep streaming after the viewer is revoked, because revocation is checked only when the request enters the middleware.

On SshBare and AwsEc2 targets, the controller records a relative dispatcher command but the worker compares it with an absolute worker_root/hel path, so the owned review dispatcher is never preapproved in Guardian mode.
truncate_line_to_width reserves one cell but appends the two-cell ASCII ellipsis "..", so truncated lines exceed their width by one.
The transcript row cache is invalidated on width, mode and theme but not on the symbol set, so open conversations keep the old glyphs after Symbols changes.
In ASCII mode a partial quota cell that rounds down draws nothing, but empty_cells still subtracts a cell, so the bar is 9 cells instead of 10.
Composer hint strings still use literal " · " but are split on footer_separator(), which is " - " in ASCII mode, so the hints become one item that keeps Unicode and is dropped as a whole.
After two failures stack, the duplicate check compares the new raw text with the formatted "N failures · latest: X" text, so a repeat of X still increments the count.
Identical failures from independent operations within the protection window are not counted as separate failures.
The stacked-failure notice hardcodes a Unicode middle dot, so it draws a non-ASCII glyph when the ASCII symbol set is active.
The Setup choices for Symbols offer only unicode and ascii, so the setting cannot return to the unset 'Follows the terminal' state.
The Recent messages log cuts every notice to one row with no wrap or expand, so the end of a long failure cannot be read.
When LC_ALL, LC_CTYPE and LANG are all unset, automatic detection chooses Unicode rather than ASCII.
Transcript entry headers take their mark from mj_client::transcript::entry_glyph, which is always Unicode, and discard the symbol-set glyph from tool_presentation.
Several other UI surfaces still draw hardcoded Unicode in ASCII mode: the microphone chip, title and empty-transcript separators, Resume dialog hints, minimized pane headings, and Help hints.
ComboBox::display_value still formats with the Unicode Self::GLYPH instead of the new glyph() helper, so Setup and wizard summaries show ▾ in ASCII mode.
In Monochrome, unfocused and disabled controls get reverse video from raised(), while the focused control's style has no REVERSED, so focus looks weaker than its neighbours.
In Monochrome, disabled controls render exactly like enabled unfocused controls.
In Monochrome, the unavailable voice button is drawn in reverse video while the available and active states are not, which inverts their emphasis.
The notice log dialog scrolls only on keys, so mouse wheel events do nothing.
When CODEX_CONFIG comes from the login shell rather than an explicit override, the pin writes a model-only object that replaces the inherited value and drops its other keys.
The model pin is written into acp-supervisor.json only at worker or reviewer launch, so an in-worker bridge restart after a model change reopens Codex on the stale pinned model.
If the recorded model has been withdrawn, the pin starts Codex on it, so queued prompts may go to an unavailable model where the session previously started on the profile default.

In a YOLO Claude session the plan-approval form still offers 'Yes, manually approve edits' (exit-plan-default), but the new branch auto-approves every later edit because permission_policy stays Unconstrained.

In YOLO Muse sessions, is_plan_permission's whole-request heuristic (title/name containing 'exitplanmode', any nested kind 'switch_mode') now exempts ordinary tool requests from auto-approval and routes them to a plan review with no plan.
YOLO auto-approvals are logged only with tracing::debug and not recorded in the durable relay as PermissionAutoApproved.

At widths of 640px or less, tabbing from an empty editor to Send or Attach removes composer-has-intent, because only editor focus counts, so the action row is hidden and keyboard users cannot reach Attach.

composerActionPointerDown is cleared only by pointerup/pointercancel on #prompt-form, so with a mouse or pen, pressing Send or Attach and releasing outside the form leaves the actions visible on an idle composer.
The commit changes viewer.html, viewer.css and viewer.js (precached shell assets) without bumping CACHE_VERSION in service-worker.js, against that file's stated rule.
The new phone header margins and padding make the global header taller, pushing the new-session wizard's first folder row below the 844px viewport and breaking an existing phone regression test.

plan-mode.spec.js reveals #subagents-button by removing its hidden class, but the button now sits inside #conversation-status, which stays display:none (status-empty) when the queue is empty, so the later toBeVisible assertion fails at 390px.
phone-layout.spec.js sets isMobile: true unconditionally, which Playwright Firefox rejects, so the new cases fail under MJ_BROWSER_ENGINE=firefox.
Focusing the empty editor grows the composer by about 80px without keeping the transcript at its tail, so a reader at the bottom falls outside atTail()'s 48px slack and stops following new output.
Claimed that the existing #conversation-side max-height: 25dvh / overflow-y: auto rule still applies on phones and nests a second scroller around the new 40dvh content.
The ExecPlan update omits the closing revision note that .agents/PLANS.md requires.
Form::hit checks controls in reverse registration order, so later-registered fields and buttons under an open combobox popup take clicks and wheel events meant for the popup.

Ctrl-S with a Setup choice popup open is routed through ComboBoxState::route, which closes the popup, but Save is ignored while an editor exists and Activate(Choices) is no longer handled, leaving a collapsed editor that cannot be reopened or accepted.
Accepting an unchanged value in a review settings combobox closes it without requesting a repaint, so the popup stays on screen while input treats it as closed.
An open Model or Effort popup keeps a numeric pending index when discovery replaces the choice list, so accepting without moving the cursor commits a different value.

delete_empty_workspace_at allows deleting the empty 'default' workspace, after which every session-context insert (which relies on the column default 'default') is rejected by the new trigger, and nothing recreates the row.

Adding a fourth session_contexts column breaks existing tests that insert three positional values into the migrated table (three findings in this group also report the version-13 fixture problem in g3).
version_thirteen_restores_checkpointed_lost_sessions_to_recoverable_errors rewinds user_version to 12 on a schema-14 database, so reopening reruns migration 14 and fails at CREATE TABLE workspaces.

assign_new_session_workspace_at reads the current workspace, checks it, and updates in separate autocommit statements, so two concurrent assignments can both pass the check and the second overwrites the first.
assign_new_session_workspace_at cannot tell a new context from an old session in 'default', so any existing default-workspace session can be moved despite the stated immutability.

The name_key CHECK limits the lowercased key to 64 characters, but Unicode lowercasing can lengthen a valid name (for example U+0130 becomes two code points), so create and rename fail for names the validator accepts.
to_lowercase is not Unicode case folding, so some case variants (Straße vs STRASSE, ς vs Σ) get different keys and can coexist despite the promised case-insensitive uniqueness.
list_workspaces counts session_contexts rows, which delete_session keeps for prompt history, so session_count includes deleted sessions.
The test legacy_sessions_are_migrated_into_the_default_workspace_without_copying_state inserts its session after migration 14 has run, so it does not exercise upgrading existing schema-13 data.

Worker source capture (copying, hashing and fsyncing up to three full worker binaries, even when already cached) runs before the daemon binds and publishes metadata, so connect_or_start's fixed 8 s START_TIMEOUT can expire and the starting command fails.

The content-addressed workers/pinned/<digest>/hel cache is never pruned, so every distinct local worker build leaves a permanent full copy and disk usage grows without bound on machines that rebuild often.

publish_cached_worker reuses an existing cache file without checking its digest, so a truncated or modified cached worker is pinned and installed in place of the freshly copied, correct bytes, and restarting cannot repair it.
A worker first captured from a non-executable source keeps that mode in the digest-keyed cache, so fixing the source's permissions and restarting still reuses the non-executable cached copy.
The ExecPlan lacks milestones and defines no terms of art.

The startup summary carries an unread count computed from the read cursor captured at dashboard start; applying it after the user has read the chat, or over an equal-ordinal live projection, restores stale unread state.

The SQL nonempty-agent predicate uses SQLite's one-argument trim(), which strips only spaces, unlike Rust's str::trim. A newline- or tab-only agent message is counted as unread, and the LIMIT 1 query then selects it and returns None instead of the previous real answer.
The last-user-message query only considers items whose stable_id starts with user: or user-, so user items with other IDs would be skipped.

load_materialized_session_summary_from runs its session-row, user, agent and ordinal queries as separate autocommit reads, so a concurrent relay-page commit can mix projection versions under the older event ordinal.
The user-message query calls json_extract without a json_valid guard, so one malformed user body makes the whole summary load fail.
A failed summary load is reported only through tracing::warn!, and no tracing subscriber is installed, so the error is effectively discarded.

The summary seeds materialized_applied_event_ordinal from the stored projection, so a live snapshot rewound by repair_projection to a lower checkpoint frontier would be rejected by the strict-ordinal guard.
A reviewer report stating that the diff has no findings.
Import uses the local HEAD as base_commit, so the committed bundle is always empty and unpushed commits are neither archived nor restorable on a fresh clone.
The new default musl build target moves release output, but README still runs ./target/release/hel.
Kimi --latest ranks sessions by the session directory mtime, which does not change when state.json or agents/main/wire.jsonl are appended or rewritten in place.
The Claude transcript reader never closes a trailing turn, so an import that ends without an end_turn assistant record replays into WorkerPhase::Running and the restored worker rejects new prompts.
The new `.unwrap_or(origin)` shorthand fallback makes non-GitHub remotes (git@gitlab.com:team/repo, ../repo, mirrors/repo) parse as GitHub owner/repository.
Defaulting build.target to x86_64-unknown-linux-musl breaks CI jobs that run plain cargo without installing that target.

The new container cleanup runs only when locator_after_provision fails, which cannot happen for container targets; failures in the Git install or clone steps after `podman run` still leave the container running.
Prepended BatchMode/StrictHostKeyChecking/ConnectTimeout defaults override user ssh_args because OpenSSH keeps the first value, contrary to the comment.
The prepended ConnectTimeout=15 beats the ConnectTimeout=3 that remote path completion appends, so Tab completion on an unreachable SSH Podman host blocks the dashboard for about 15 seconds.
unique_bundle_id adds an `import-` prefix and numeric suffix to a base of up to 64 characters, producing IDs that fail validate_id.
`hel import` loads and saves a whole HelState copy without coordinating with a running dashboard/server, so either writer's next save can drop the other's session records.
Import calls collect_git_snapshot without the reject_dirty_submodules guard, so dirty submodule work is silently missing from a verified archive.
A parse error in the first eight lines of any Codex rollout aborts discovery, blocking import of every other session, including by explicit ID.
Claude user records whose message.content is an array (for example text plus an image) are dropped entirely from the canonical transcript.
Claim that `--session` with Kimi's session ID never matches because candidates keep the `session_` prefix.
Claim that a relative or tilde workspace path gives the wrong Claude slug or Kimi hash on restore.
active_lifecycles now locks self.controller, but session_projection already holds that std Mutex when it calls it, so the first web/phone publish self-deadlocks and keeps the controller locked.

The new cancellation gate reads the daemon's cached controller, while the close persists Destroying through its own separately loaded Controller, so Alt-X during the cache lag (or just before the transition) can still kill target teardown.

When the newly routed Stop retry goes through recover_interrupted_close_managed and fails after Destroying is persisted (last_error cleared), the error is not recorded, so the TUI no longer sees a failed transition and blocks Stop again.
The web/phone Cancel path calls cancel_lifecycle_if_active, which skips the new Destroying gate, so a stale or racing web Cancel can still interrupt a close past its checkpoint.
Claim that session_transition_commands_bind_no_key restates the command list instead of testing key input, against the repository test rule.

The new post-stop check pipes `ps -eo args=` into `grep -F -- "$hel_match"`, and grep's own argv contains the expanded pattern, so it can match itself and report 'worker still running after stop' after a successful stop.
`model: "current"` and effort inheritance read only `operational.config`, which `SessionConfigured` does not fill, so a parent on its harness default model gets 'current model is unknown'.

Explicit and inherited effort is checked against the chosen profile's default-model effort list, not the requested model's, so valid efforts are rejected or dropped and invalid ones are passed on and fail the child's startup.

Spawn now waits for every eligible profile's discovery (up to 240 s in the worker, 300 s process deadline), which can outlast the MCP shim's 120 s spawn reply timeout, so the parent gets a tool error with no child ID while the daemon may still create the child.
A spawn that pins `profile_id` still waits for discovery of every unrelated eligible profile before the pin is honoured.

For a Muse profile whose bridge exposes no model selector, discovery synthesizes the model from settings.json, and the now-mandatory model is passed to apply_followup, which requires it in the live config options and fails before the prompt.

When a spawn request is replayed and registration returns the existing child, the follow-up uses a freshly re-resolved selection (which now depends on quota and discovery) instead of the stored relation's model and effort.

Selection now runs before the delegation policy check, so with `[subagents] enabled = false` the HTTP spawn reports 'no eligible profile offers model' instead of 'sub-agents are disabled'; a session forced on (`mjolnir_subagents = Some(true)`) is refused when it was allowed before.
An older worker still running after a daemon upgrade can send a spawn with no model, which the new daemon rejects.

load_report_state and WaitObservation::apply_subagent_report pass only the active turn as in_flight, so a reminder still queued after the 30 s grace reads as Fallback and the wait completes with the old last message.
The session wait loop has no timer for the end of the reminder grace (or a DB-only reminder-failure record), so a live idle child can make `mj wait` time out instead of returning the fallback report.

A handback request carries no turn identity; the daemon attributes it to whatever turn is active when it processes the request, so a request that outlives its MCP timeout can land on a later turn or be refused with no turn running.

When the completion hook skips the reminder because something is queued, it still marks the turn noticed; if the queue drains without a new turn (a SetConfig entry, or a removed prompt), report_state stays Pending{remind:true} forever and both waits report the idle child as running.
Reminder admission uses the in_flight list captured from the earlier snapshot, so a prompt admitted during the job's awaits gets an obsolete reminder queued behind it.
A reminder the worker accepted but whose acknowledgement was lost is recorded as failed, so waits fall back to the old last message while the reminder still runs.

After a steer, the projected active turn takes the queued prompt's command id while the turn completes under the original prompt id, so a handback recorded during a steered turn never matches the finished turn.
subagent_handbacks rows have no foreign key or cleanup on the session-deletion path, so destroyed children's reports accumulate.

hel_kill_tree sends KILL to every snapshotted PGID, including a legacy worker's inherited group, bypassing the hel_group=legacy PID-only fallback and possibly killing unrelated processes in that group.
Processes that a tree member starts in a new process group after the one-time snapshot are not tracked, so the stop can succeed while they still write.
hel_tree_running checks only snapshotted PIDs, not snapshotted groups, so a post-snapshot child that stays in a snapshotted group survives if its parent exits during the TERM grace.
Snapshotted PIDs and PGIDs are signalled after the grace without a birth-identity check, so a reused PID could be killed.
hel_snapshot_tree turns a ps or awk failure into an empty tree and hel_stop ignores it, so a failed snapshot silently falls back to group-only waiting.
The new test starts an endless setsid harness without a cleanup guard, so a failed assertion before or during the stop leaves it running.

The launch config sends only the file name of the authentication marker, so Kimi's nested credentials/kimi-code.json becomes kimi-code.json at the root of the staged home and credential sync uses the wrong file.
fetch_catalog_over_https uses reqwest::blocking inside a Tokio context on the sub-agent and resume paths, which panics when the client's runtime is dropped.
Catalog cache rows use the same (profile, "") primary key as default-model discovery rows, so discovery and catalog staging overwrite each other.
A successful HTTP response is cached before it is parsed, so an invalid 200 body replaces the last good catalog and the launch fails without trying the cached copy.
The catalog download reads the whole body with no size limit.
The catalog parser accepts only Codex's {"models": [...]} shape, so a custom provider whose /models returns the OpenAI {"data": [...]} list cannot launch or be discovered.

A custom provider that uses experimental_bearer_token instead of env_key gets no generated catalog, and validation forbids a user-supplied model_catalog_json, so it keeps OpenAI's built-in model names.
Reviewer staging calls stage_profile without stage_codex_catalog, so a custom-provider Codex reviewer has no models.json, offers OpenAI model names, and gets no Guardian reviewer stamp.
ZCode quota refresh now always returns an 'unsupported' error while the ZCode harness still exists.
Building quota refresh requests and credential sync targets now reads each Codex profile's config.toml synchronously on the TUI and server event loops.
For an API-key profile, reconcile_session still reads the native auth.json before the API-key guard, so an unreadable or directory auth.json aborts skills and GitHub-token sync.
The catalog fallback reads the shared cache, which ignores rows older than 24 hours, so an outage more than a day after the last successful fetch blocks launch.
If the user's config.toml is not owner-writable, the staged copy keeps that mode and the in-place write that prepends model_catalog_json fails.
point_config_at_catalog treats any read error on the staged config.toml as an empty file.

When a native Codex profile switches to a custom provider, its cached CodexUsageClient (a live codex app-server child) is returned unused and kept until the profile is removed or the controller exits.
The quota refresher snapshots the provider into QuotaRefreshRequest and republishes only when the HarnessProfile map changes, so editing only config.toml leaves periodic quota on the old path.

The restore seed reads only the literal keys model and effort from the archived configuration, which the projection keys by the harness's option ID, so selectors such as Codex's reasoning_effort are dropped on a native resume.
The archived configuration holds every advertised current value, including defaults the user never accepted, so seeding from it can pin the old profile's default model as accepted.
